speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
text: asked the Minister for Law regarding unauthorised access to a vendor-managed Singapore Land Authority test environment containing real personal data of about 70,000 individuals (a) how did the data enter and remain in a dataset intended for mock or anonymised data; (b) when was the environment last audited against Government data-security requirements; and (c) what contractual action will be considered after investigations.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: First, will SLA also be undertaking audits of any other development or test environments arising from this incident to make sure that no similar issues are occurring elsewhere?

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And secondly, it seems like the Senior Minister of State has acknowledged that the audits that were previously undertaken might have had some gaps, and especially, it sounds like the audits were being undertaken on the nature of the technical controls, but not of the actual data, given that the data set has been in existence for almost 20 years and it was only uncovered now.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Will SLA reform their audit process going forward, so that the actual data is audited periodically, to make sure that no personal information inside is leaked?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Based on the IT risk landscape known at that time, the audit prioritised broader information and communications technology (ICT) security and resilience controls, such as cloud security management, privileged access and third party management.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This is something that we can consider once the investigation is complete.
